title: Identifying members in the Absinthe House band photo
summary: Looking at photographs, he names Warnick, Johnny Lindsey, Steve Lewis, his brother Charlie, the Newmans and Henry Martin, and recalls two years on WWL and three at the Absinthe House.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: So, Warnick didn't play clarinet at the time?

No, he was playing saxophone alto. Only. But he played clarinet. He taught him in other ways. T.O. taught him. Mm-hmm. And who's the sousaphone player? This fellow here. He's in New York now. He's a British subject. A.C. Gary is his name. A.C. Gary? Yeah, this is Johnny Lindsey. He played the trombone.
He died in Chicago. That's Steve Lewis.
That's my brother, Charlie. And that's me there, see? Mm-hmm. That's the same band.
Now here's the, here's the crew old Saturdays in the Absinthe House. We stayed two years on WWL with that band.
Now we have a violin player here and a trumpet player.
That's your both. That's my brother there. He's in California now. He's a sousaphone player.
What is his name? Henry. And that's Warnick? That's Warnick, yeah.
And this? That's Joe Newman, he's playing with bass in our bass. That's his daddy, Dwight Newman. And the drummer?

Henry Martin. Mm-hmm. And that's Charlie, my brother there. That's the old Absinthe House. See that rail you've been in there, eh? Mm-hmm. That old rail and everything. We stayed there for three years in that job. They were dancing there then, you know?
